transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Aster Procurement), Diego Ruiz (Aster Legal), Chen Wei (Aster Infra)

Summary: quick workshop to align MSA/DPA exceptions, billing and SSO/KMS scope for a pilot. goal is to confirm path to pilot and deadlines for redlines and security docs.

00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off. appreciate you carving out the time. quick roll call?
00:12 - Nora Patel: Nora here, procurement.
00:15 - Diego Ruiz: Diego, legal.
:18 - Chen Wei: Chen, infra team.
00:21 - Liam O'Rourke: Liam from Redwood infra.

00:30 - Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda — align on MSA redlines, DPA scope (data residency/encryption/KMS), SLA expectations and billing path for the pilot. also a bit on whether private deployment is necessary vs hosted with VPC controls.
00:48 - Nora Patel: Our procurement committee flagged three main things — one: we need clarity on data residency and retention in the DPA, two: billing model needs to map to our PO cadence (monthly vs quarterly), and three: any KMS/HSM integration — we need to know who holds keys.
01:10 - Diego Ruiz: From legal — we have a couple standard redlines around indemnity and export control language. also want to confirm audit rights and subprocessor list.
01:26 - Chen Wei: Technical: we care about VPC peering, private deployment or dedicated capacity; we run some sensitive workloads and would prefer customer-managed keys if possible. also curious about perf for 4k token seqs, latency 95th perc needs to be under 400ms for interactive apps.

01:45 - Liam O'Rourke: okay, noted. quick framing — Redwood offers hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem. For pilot we usually recommend hosted with VPC/network isolation first unless you have strict regulatory needs. If you need customer-managed KMS that's supported on Private and on Dedicated via our KMS integrations.
02:10 - Nora Patel: Our procurement prefers not to sign on-prem contracts for the pilot — they'd rather test hosted or dedicated. But the KMS thing is a blocker: we have corporate policy that keys must be customer-managed for certain data classes.
02:27 - Maya Chen: Understood. We can run a pilot in Dedicated with a customer-managed KMS — that's often the middle ground. we'll surface the KMS integration doc after this call.
02:42 - Diego Ruiz: Can you point me to the MSA clause that covers data processor vs controller? I saw a section but the wording looked, uh, broad.
02:52 - Maya Chen: yeah, the current MSA uses processor language; we can flag the exact section in the redline. we'll highlight responsibilities around PII vs anonymized inference.
03:05 - Chen Wei: about the latency target — do you have published perf numbers for the model variants? we need numbers to map to our SLOs.
03:14 - Liam O'Rourke: We have model performance profiles. for example, the redwood-medium-v2 (approx 7B) in dedicated configs typically lands at ~120-180ms p95 for 512 tokens on an A100 type host under steady load; for longer sequences 2-4k it's higher, obviously. we'll send a condensed benchmark sheet.
03:36 - Diego Ruiz: on audit — we'll need SOC 2 and any FedRAMP or ISO statements you have, and a subprocessor list.
03:45 - Maya Chen: absolutely. i'll attach SOC2 report and our security packet. note: FedRAMP we don't have (for hosted) but we can discuss enterprise Private pathway.

04:05 - Nora Patel: billing — our finance team requires the MSA to specify invoicing cadence and a PR number flow. is there flexibility on monthly invoicing for pilots?
04:15 - Maya Chen: yes, pilots are typically billed monthly. if you eventually move to committed reserved capacity the contracts are quarterly/annual. we can include language in the SOW to state monthly invoicing for the pilot and list the PO workflow.

04:35 - Diego Ruiz: about liability caps — the MSA has a standard cap equal to fees paid in 12 months. we might ask for an exceptions path if we move to a larger committed deal.
04:46 - Maya Chen: that's common; we can note that exceptions are escalated to commercial/legal and we'll fast-track for enterprise deals. but initial cap for pilot tends to remain standard.

05:02 - Chen Wei: KMS again — if keys are managed by us, can you confirm no key material leaves our control and that logs are provided for KMS operations?
05:12 - Liam O'Rourke: yes — with customer-managed KMS the keys are in your KMS and we use envelope encryption; key material never leaves your HSM. we can produce key rotation logs / KMS audit hooks as part of the integration. we'll share the integration spec.
05:30 - Diego Ruiz: subprocessors — can you provide the current list and the policy for adding new subprocessors? our procurement wants notice and a right to object for high-risk subprocessors.
05:44 - Maya Chen: we have a subprocessor list in the security packet and a 30-day notice process for new ones, with an objection window. we'll surface that in the DPA section.

06:00 - Nora Patel: internal approvals also ask if there's a pass-through termination clause in case of export controls or sanctions — we need clarity.
06:10 - Diego Ruiz: yes, export controls are big for us; can you confirm any geographic restrictions or flow of data to third countries?
06:19 - Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted regions are in US/EU/APAC. we can control region of processing for your tenant. any export controls would be handled per the DPA; we'll call out region restrictions in the SOW.

06:35 - Chen Wei: about private deployment — if we do that later, do you have an on-prem package and support SLA?
06:42 - Liam O'Rourke: we do. on-prem/private includes a customer-managed control plane and optional remote support. SLA tiers vary by deployment; we can map a dedicated SLA for latency and uptime in the SOW.
06:58 - Nora Patel: procurement question — what approvals are needed from your side to do MSA exceptions? timeline?
07:05 - Maya Chen: typical internal path: AE triages, legal reviews redlines, then commercial approves fee/terms. for low-risk redlines we can often sign within 2 weeks; for substantive indemnity or export control changes it can extend to 3-4 weeks. we'll aim for the 2-week path for the pilot.
07:25 - Diego Ruiz: okay that's helpful. any examples of prior enterprise redlines you accepted?
07:31 - Maya Chen: yes — we've accepted limited indemnity carve-outs for specific regulated customers, and we've done narrower data residency commitments. i'll share anonymized examples in the packet.

08:00 - Liam O'Rourke: switching to billing detail: your PO cadence — monthly invoicing ok? do you require NET30? NET45?
08:08 - Nora Patel: standard for us is NET30 but we can do NET45 for pilots if needed. our AP team will confirm.
08:15 - Maya Chen: noted. we'll draft SOW billing language: monthly invoices, payment terms NET30. 

08:30 - Diego Ruiz: cross-border data transfers — if we elect to process in EU only, how do you support that?
08:38 - Liam O'Rourke: we can pin the tenant to an EU region; our DPA supports region binding for certain accounts. for backups and support telemetry we can agree on data flows in the DPA.

08:55 - Chen Wei: perf benchmarks — can we do a quick discussion on how you measure p95 for interactive vs batch? i want to ensure our test harness maps to your internal metric.
09:04 - Liam O'Rourke: we measure p95 at the request layer excluding network egress for same-VPC deployments; for hosted public endpoints there's some network variance. for pilot we'll run tests from your infra and ours to normalize.

09:28 - Maya Chen: i see a question about SLA credits — are credits applied to future invoices?
09:35 - Diego Ruiz: yes, practical question for procurement.
09:38 - Maya Chen: SLA credits are typically applied as billing credits on next invoice period. we can draft explicit remedy language in the SOW.

09:50 - Nora Patel: one more procurement ask — do you support consolidated invoicing across subsidiaries? we have three legal entities that will be using the service.
09:59 - Maya Chen: yes, we can issue consolidated invoices or separate invoices per entity; that will be a billing setup item. sales operations will confirm in the redlined MSA.

10:12 - Diego Ruiz: around liability — if we push for a higher cap for a committed deal, what's the negotiation posture?
10:19 - Maya Chen: fairly standard — we can increase caps in exchange for committed spend/longer term. commercial will present options based on spend bands.

10:30 - Chen Wei: technical pilot plan — we want dedicated testing for model latency at 4k tokens and KV cache behavior with session affinity. can Redwood support a short private test or do you recommend dedicated nodes?
10:43 - Liam O'Rourke: For those workloads we recommend dedicated reserved capacity. we can provision a small pool for pilot with predictable perf. otherwise a private deployment for full KMS control. we'll propose a dedicated pilot config in the perf plan.

11:05 - Nora Patel: timeline — procurement needs the redline before our 12/15 committee meeting. can you commit to sending materials earlier?
11:12 - Maya Chen: yes, target sending redlined MSA/DPA + SOC2 + subprocessor list by 12/03. that gives you time to circulate.
11:20 - Diego Ruiz: and if we want to add SSO/SAML integration, is that in scope for pilot?
11:27 - Liam O'Rourke: SSO/SAML is standard; we'll provide SAML metadata and test plan. integration usually takes 2-3 days for the pilot.

11:40 - Maya Chen: ok quick recap — deliverables from Redwood: redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2 pack, subprocessor list, KMS integration doc, perf benchmark plan, proposed SOW with billing language. from Aster: procurement checklist, PO cadence confirmation, legal redlines to the DPA.
12:00 - Nora Patel: sounds good. we'll aim to review the redlines and get comments by 12/10.
12:08 - Diego Ruiz: one last question — do you have an established escalation path for security incidents and required notification windows?
12:15 - Liam O'Rourke: yes we have incident response SLA — typically 24-hour initial notification for severity 1, with follow-up cadence. we'll include that in the security packet.
12:28 - Chen Wei: can you also confirm support hours for the pilot?
12:33 - Maya Chen: standard is business hours support; for pilots we can arrange extended overlap windows if needed. we'll outline that in the SOW.

12:50 - Maya Chen: thanks all. we'll send the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff meeting for the week of 12/08. any objections?
12:58 - Nora Patel: no objections. thanks.
13:03 - Diego Ruiz: thanks everyone.
13:06 - Meeting close.

Notes/links referenced:
- Security packet (SOC2 report, subprocessor list): https://redwood.example.com/security-packet/ast2026 (placeholder)
